summary: This article explains why the ancient Egyptians built the pyramids of Giza, how paid workers moved and raised millions of heavy stone blocks, and why the Great Pyramid still amazes the world.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “The Pyramids of Egypt” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: from a time very, very long ago
a light-colored stone that is often used for building
a large, open place where stone is dug or cut out of the ground

challengeTerms.def: a large structure built to honor a person or event, or one that is important in history
a large, organized society with its own cities, government, and culture
a scientist who studies the past by digging up and examining old objects and places

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that people long ago were just as clever as people today? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the ancient Egyptians moved such heavy stones without modern machines.
struggling: Pre-teach ancient, limestone, and quarry with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses monument, civilization, and archaeologist to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
